title: Chart the monthly revenue trend
scenario:
Kabir is presenting at the monthly business review and wants one slide showing how FY2024-25 went month by month. He wants the audience to see the festive peak and the year-end sale at a glance.

> "Give me one chart of monthly net revenue for last financial year. Delivered orders, India time. Pick whatever chart makes the shape obvious."
task:
1. Write a query that returns **one row per month** of FY2024-25 (April 2024 to March 2025, IST) with the month and the **net revenue of Delivered orders**. Remember the data quirks from lab 1.
2. Run it, then choose the **chart type** and the **x and y fields** that best show the trend.
3. Submit. The grader checks both your numbers and your chart choice.
hints: Convert to IST first, then bucket: `DATE_TRUNC('month', order_ts_utc + INTERVAL 330 MINUTE)` or `strftime(order_ts_utc + INTERVAL 330 MINUTE, '%Y-%m')`.
Same cleaning as lab 1: `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM orders` before summing.
Which chart is built for *change over an ordered time axis*? Bars compare categories; slices of a pie compare parts of a whole.
explanation:
**Data:** convert to IST before truncating to the month, de-duplicate, and keep only Delivered orders. Twelve rows, one per month.

**Chart:** a **line chart** (or area) is the standard for a trend over an ordered time axis: the eye follows the slope, so the October festive peak and March's year-end bump jump out. Bars work but emphasise individual months over the shape. A pie chart hides order completely; nobody can read a trend from twelve slices.

At work, also start the y-axis at zero for areas and bars (lines can start elsewhere if you label clearly) and annotate the Diwali peak.
interview:
*"For a monthly business review I built a revenue trend in SQL, converting UTC timestamps to IST before bucketing by month so the festive spike landed in the right month, and used a line chart with the Diwali peak annotated. The discussion moved straight to why November softened versus October rather than debating the numbers."*

Expect: **"When would you NOT use a line chart?"** (Unordered categories; very few points; part-to-whole.)

typeFeedback.bar: Bars can show monthly values, but they emphasise individual months over the shape of the trend. For change over time, a line reads faster.
typeFeedback.pie: A pie chart shows parts of a whole and throws away the time order, so the trend disappears.
typeFeedback.scatter: A scatter plot is for the relationship between two numeric measures, not a trend over months.
